precepts.point: With the same tongue they murmur and slander; they are carnal and not about the unity of the faith. Mark them.

precepts.text: Murmuring is venom: an unverified report sown in you changes how you see leadership and spreads spiritual decay.
precepts.point: With the same tongue they murmur and slander; they are carnal and not about the unity of the faith. Mark them.

precepts.text: Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour; remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance. Sometimes brothers and sisters do something simple; wink at it. It does not always have to be a counsel for small matters. Abstain from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sins. If thou blow the spark, it shall burn: if thou spit upon it, it shall be quenched: and both these come out of thy mouth. A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: we just read that Onias had to flee from Jerusalem to Syria. It hath pulled down strong cities, and overthrown the houses of great men.
precepts.point: Not only the Jews, but many also of other nations, took great indignation, and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man, because Onias had a good report even among the other nations. The king was heartily sorry, and moved to pity, and wept, because of the sober and modest behaviour of him that was dead; and being kindled with anger, he took away Andronicus his purple, rent off his clothes, led him through the whole city unto that very place where he had committed impiety against Onias, and there slew he the cursed murderer. Thus the Lord rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved.
precepts.why:
When Onias found out Menelaus was stealing vessels of gold out of the temple, he reproved him and had to run for his life, fleeing from Jerusalem up to the sanctuary at Daphne by Antiochia in Syria. Sirach shows what drives a man like that from his place.

“Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.” Sometimes brothers and sisters may do something simple. Wink at it. It doesn't always have to be a counsel for small matters. “Abstain from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sins: for a furious man will kindle strife”, and “A sinful man disquieteth friends, and maketh debate among them that be at peace.”

“An hasty contention kindleth a fire: and an hasty fighting sheddeth blood. If thou blow the spark, it shall burn: if thou spit upon it, it shall be quenched: and both these come out of thy mouth.” Your mouth has the power: you can blow on that spark and it will burn, or you can spit on it, let it go, and quench it.

“Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace. A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation”. We just read that Onias had to flee from Jerusalem up to Syria. “strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.” A backbiting tongue overthrew the house of a great man, Onias, the real high priest.

precepts.text: A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many; strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men. Somebody that lies on you can do much destruction.
precepts.point: His master's wrath was kindled, and Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were bound. Remember how old Joseph is: 17.
precepts.why:
When Potiphar’s wife could not get her way, she lied. She called the men of her house and said, “See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us; he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice.” Then “she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home”: she kept his clothes as false evidence, and told her husband the same lie.

Sirach shows what that kind of tongue does: “A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.” Somebody that lies on you can do much destruction. Joseph was the greatest man in Potiphar's house, trusted with everything, and a lying tongue brought him down to the king's prison.

It is the same today. Many brothers have been locked up because a woman lied on them: an ex-wife or ex-girlfriend who wants his life to go down the tubes, who calls him over, is refused, and then threatens to tell the police he hurt her. Others are in jail because a woman started a fight and expected him to defend her. Don't deal with a woman like that; that is the kind of woman Joseph had over him.

And this same spirit met our people in slavery. A lot of us were put to death because of it. Emmett Till was put to death for the lying woman, and there are a lot of cases like that. What Potiphar's wife did to Joseph, a backbiting tongue has done to Israel again and again.

precepts.text: Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue. The tongue does a lot of evil, and that's what Potiphar's wife did to Joseph.
precepts.point: His master's wrath was kindled, and Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were bound. Remember how old Joseph is: 17.
precepts.why:
Sirach goes on: “Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.” The tongue does a lot of evil, and that is exactly what Potiphar’s wife did to Joseph. She never lifted a sword against him; she only spoke, and her words did the work.

She told her husband, “The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me,” and “when his master heard the words of his wife,” “his wrath was kindled.” On nothing but her word, “Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound.” Remember how old Joseph is here: 17.

That is how our people have fallen too: brothers in prison on a lie, and in slavery times men like Emmett Till put to death because of a lying woman's words. More have fallen by the tongue than by the sword. Guard yourself from the kind of company that can destroy you with a word.

This explains winking at ignorance. “Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth”. You poke my eye, I poke out yours; you knock out my tooth, I knock out yours. That was the law.

“But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.” That is winking at ignorance.

Turning the other cheek does not mean you stand there and let somebody abuse you and beat you up. That is the Christian way of thinking. Somebody tries to punch you in the face, you better block that; self-defence is right. What Christ is saying is be willing to forgive that person.

This is the key thing with repentance. “Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him”. If your brother did evil against you, rebuke him: bro, you were wrong for what you did, don’t do that again.

“And if he repent, forgive him.” The key word is if he repent. Forgiveness comes with repentance: for me to forgive you, you have to repent and say, I’m sorry.

If he will not repent, the Bible shows how to deal with him: bring two or three witnesses; if he won’t hear them, bring him before the congregation; if he won’t hear the congregation, deal with him as an heathen and a publican. Cut him off.

“Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?” “I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.” That is four hundred and ninety times. If he comes and acknowledges what he did wrong and says he is sorry, you have to forgive him. You cannot say, I don’t think he really repented, so I’m not forgiving him. You want a good conscience before God.

But forgiveness and repentance go both ways. A sister tells another sister her personal business in confidence, and she goes gossiping. You rebuke her, she says I’m sorry, and you must forgive her. But would you still tell her your personal business? You would be an idiot. She broke your trust, and she has to win it back. When you hurt somebody and they forgive you, you have to prove yourself to them again and gain back their trust.

“So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.” From your hearts, not from your mouth. You can say I forgive you while deep down you are still carrying secret hatred, a grudge for what that person did, and you don’t want to let it go even though they said they were sorry.

To forgive from your heart is to forgive and forget: you don’t hold on to it anymore, you heal from the hurt they did to you. If you don’t forgive from the heart, the Lord will destroy you. And the Lord sees your heart, whether you really forgave that person.

“A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle.” If you lie on somebody and offend them, it is going to be hard to win back that person’s trust, but you have to try. And if that brother or sister sincerely forgave you, they will open the gates back up and let you in.

So in offence and forgiveness both parties have work to do. The one who forgives must make sure they forgive from the heart, and the one who was forgiven has to win back the love of that person.

“He that revengeth shall find vengeance from the Lord”. We are supposed to understand that among our own people, and so with the enemy, because the Lord said vengeance belongs to him. That is why we wait for him, and he rewards them that wait.

precepts.why:
Y’all see what one little lie can do: it can destroy. “Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace.” “A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.” That is what a backbiting tongue, gossip, a lie, can do.

“A backbiting tongue hath cast out virtuous women, and deprived them of their labours. Whoso hearkeneth unto it shall never find rest, and never dwell quietly.” Don’t listen to lies, don’t listen to gossip; that is what God is telling us, avoid it.

“The stroke of the whip maketh marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaketh the bones.” When people say sticks and stones may break my bones but words can never hurt me, that’s a lie. Words can hurt you; words can break bones. “Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.” People telling lies against people have gotten many people killed and put out of their homes and houses.

That gossip YouTuber who was sued for millions for slander and lost the case is the proof of it, and now another celebrity is suing her. Y’all think them videos is funny, but when you run around repeating that stuff you will get in trouble behind it, and God ain’t with you: Lord, why am I in trouble? Because you didn’t obey what I told you. Let others gossip; we should not be involved in gossip. Stay in the scriptures, don’t add to what an article says and don’t take away from it, and don’t take it personal when somebody talks crap about us. It’s bigger than you.

Christ forgave us out of many idolatrous things and many sins, outside and inside this truth; we have to forgive our brothers the same way if we want that forgiveness.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour; remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance: if somebody offends you, brush it off your shoulders and let it go.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: Abstain from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sins: for a furious man will kindle strife. A sinful man disquieteth friends, and maketh debate among them that be at peace: wherever the bitter brother goes he brings debate and chaos, vain arguments with no fruit. When it says disquiet, that is the feeling when the brother comes around and your defenses go up, because only bitter brothers come with strife; the brothers with peace come with the fruit of the spirit.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: He that revengeth shall find vengeance from the Lord, and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance. If you take vengeance, you will find vengeance from the Lord. If David had taken vengeance, he would have found vengeance from the Lord.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Forgive thy neighbour the hurt that he hath done unto thee, so shall thy sins also be forgiven when thou prayest. We will do things that hurt each other from time to time; your spouse will do things that hurt you from time to time. Why does it say the hurt? Because it hurts, and you do not really want to forgive; it is hard. But you have to do what God says and get rid of that pride, because if you do not forgive them, it turns into bitterness. And it is not talking about forgiving only the small things you want to forgive; it is talking about the stuff that really hurt. King David forgave Saul for trying to kill him.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Weigh thy words in a balance: make sure you check yourself before you wreck yourself. You may need to check yourself before you open your mouth and speak some evil.
And make a door and bar for thy mouth: the scripture said make a door and bar for your big mouth. Watch what you say, cuz it could get you lake of fire.
If thou blow the spark, it shall burn: if thou spit upon it, it shall be quenched. You don't got to do all that. You don't got to be murmuring, backbiting, gossiping.
Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace. You go back sowing discord between your brother or your sister, that's abomination to the Lord.

A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: backbiting tongue will drive you from nation to nation. Strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men. What do you think will happen in your congregation? Your congregation can be in disarray because of backbiting and murmuring.
Whoso hearkeneth unto it shall never find rest: if somebody come to you gossiping, backbiting, and you hearken unto it, scripture say you ain't going to find rest.
The stroke of the tongue breaketh the bones: you got to watch what you say. Remember the scripture say you going to be held accountable for every idle word.
Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.
And weigh thy words in a balance: weigh your words in the balance.
And make a door and bar for thy mouth.
Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: you whisper, girl, sis, you know that sister... That's what you're doing. Curse the whisperer.

For such have destroyed many that were at peace: you at peace. You don't know what the hell going on. You at peace, somebody bring you some crap they heard from three other sisters about you. You sowing discord. Gossip sows discord.

A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many: a backbiting tongue has caused issues with those that didn't even know they had issues. Didn't even know their name was being spread around like a virus. But you did that.
Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: curse the whisperer and the double tongue.

For such have destroyed many that were at peace: you have brothers and sisters that's just trying to get on in this truth. But you got brothers and sisters that are whisperers, murmurers, and complainers. Is that the people that's in your circle? Do leadership talk about people in your circle? Do leadership exhort people that's in your circle? Or are you always seeing the leadership exhort brothers and sisters that are not in the circle that you're in?
These are the things that you need to examine to know who you have around you and who you are aligning yourself with. Every beast love its own kind.

“He that revengeth shall find vengeance from the Lord”. As we read, thou shalt not avenge nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people. If your brother did something evil to you and you go back and do evil to him, God will bring vengeance on you. “And he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.” God will remember your sin any time you take vengeance.

“Forgive thy neighbour the hurt that he hath done unto thee”. Put emphasis on the hurt. People are going to hurt you. Wives might hurt their husbands, husbands their wives. A brother might step out and commit fornication on his wife, and she is going to feel hurt. A brother might carry a false report to leadership and lie on you, and it hurts. But God says forgive thy neighbour the hurt. Your neighbour first and foremost is your spouse; your neighbour is your brother, your race, your people. We have to learn to forgive each other.

“So shall thy sins also be forgiven when thou prayest.” That is the only way God will forgive you when you pray. When you sin against your God, you hurt him; he is a jealous God. Yet your brother did ought against you and you can’t forgive him, but you want God to forgive you?

In this truth there has been much hurt from people, enough to say, I ain’t messing with none of these dudes no more. But you have to forgive. The Bishop taught years ago the three trials of faith: personal, marital and congregational. Congregational is when someone among you offends you; marital is when your husband says something hurtful. Will you forgive, or shut yourself down and carry secret hatred? Each of us has to decide whether we will apply what this Bible says.
“One man beareth hatred against another, and doth he seek pardon from the Lord?” You carry secret hatred against somebody, and you want God to forgive you?

“He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and doth he ask forgiveness of his own sins?” You don’t even show mercy to a man who is just like you, and you want forgiveness for the evil you did.

“If he that is but flesh nourish hatred, who will intreat for pardon of his sins?” To nourish hatred is to feed it secretly: you keep talking about it, I can’t stand that, he did this to me again. If you hold on to it and say, I will never forgive you, not until I die, the Lord will say, then you will die with that hatred.

“Remember thy end, and let enmity cease”. Let hatred cease. We all have to die eventually. What sense is there in living on this earth hating everybody all the time, when eventually I die like everybody else and have to go before my maker? Let hatred go. “Remember corruption and death, and abide in the commandments.”

“Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to thy neighbour”: don’t bear secret hatred towards your neighbour. “Remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.” Ignorance is when your brother is ignorant, he doesn’t understand. When somebody does something hurtful or stupid to you, you have to wink at it.
